findings.issue: `tee -a` appends right after the current last byte of /etc/apt/apt.conf. If that file lacked a trailing newline, the conf's first `//` comment line would join the previous line. Today this is harmless (a `//` comment after a `;` still parses, and branch CI 44675074553 passed), but it depends on the comment being first.
findings.evidence: tools/ci/apt-network.conf:1 is a `//` comment; apt-config dump on the runner shows all three values (CI 44675074553 green).
findings.fix: Optional: leave it as it is. The comment-first layout already makes it safe. Do not add a guard.

summary: Round 2 reviews fix commit a9117d4 only. Round 1 had no blocking findings. The fix brief's MAJOR (SPEC-07 Acquire::Retries not effective on the runner) is resolved. The step keeps the same name and position, has one run line and no `if:`, and now appends tools/ci/apt-network.conf to /etc/apt/apt.conf. apt reads that file after every Dir::Etc::parts fragment, so its values win, and the conf file is still the single source of the values. The SPEC-06 static test pins the new run line exactly. The name/run/next-step regex and the ordering, value-range and budget checks are unchanged and still fail on a broken step or conf. SPEC-07's assertion is unchanged (toContain on the exact three lines). Only its failure message changed: it now lists every dump line matching /Acquire::(Retries|https?::Timeout)/, as the brief asked. README now says 'appends ... to /etc/apt/apt.conf'. No stale 99-ci-network or apt.conf.d references remain in README, .github, tools or tests. Locally, `npx vitest run tests/ci` passed: 11 files, 57 tests passed and 6 skipped (Linux-only), with the locked workflow.test.ts included. Gate fix-3 passes at 258/260 lines and 6/6 files, and branch CI 44675074553 passed with SPEC-07 running. One MINOR finding: the spec text still describes the old `sudo install` run line, and the deviation is recorded only in fix-brief.md. One NIT. There are no BLOCKER or MAJOR findings.
